text:
oncall-bot: 🚨 ALERT: eu-west1 GPU pool at 98% utilization, queue length ~1200, p99 gen latency >8s. Automatic traffic steering initiated to fallback regions. Pager: @sophie (primary oncall)

sophie: I'm on it. Pulling dashboards now. Seeing sustained enqueue rate ~600 req/s for large-context models. Dedicated customers not impacted afaict.

maya: Noted — sounds like autoscaler attempted new nodes but hit quota/limits. I'll open infra ticket.

raj: Paging in from handoff. Key questions: are failures 503s or degraded latency? Any model mismatch errors in the fallback region?

sophie: Mix of both. Most requests are queued then timed out (generated 504s) for long-generation jobs. Small fraction of requests routed to apac fallback show model-compat errors: 

```
ERROR: model_variant_mismatch: requested=redwood/gptx-1.2, available=gptx-1.2-quant, fallback_behavior=reject
Stack: runtime/router.go:421
```

sophie: That mismatch is causing immediate rejects when steering hits apac. Need config change to allow compatible variants or route to us-central instead.

infra-sre: Confirmed autoscaler tried to provision +10 nodes in eu-west1 around 1843000900 but cloud returned `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` and then `ZONE_CONSTRAINED`. Provider also returned ephemeral 'no host' for A2-type GPUs. Logs: `gce: Insufficient resources in zone eu-west1-b`

maya: I've just requested an emergency quota bump and cross-zone provisioning. Provider response time will be ~20-40m. Meanwhile we should slow enqueue and increase steer to us-central that has spare capacity.

tom: Quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce non-critical throughput (batch/async) via per-tenant throttles; 2) reroute a slice (~40%) to us-central; 3) relax model variant checks for compatible quantized variants in apac (as fallback) — with QA guardrails.

sophie: Starting step 1 now. Applying temporary rate-limits for free-tier and low-tier customers. Command: 

```sh
curl -XPOST https://control.internal/limits -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"scope":"org:free,org:starter","gen_qps":0.5}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout started: throttles -> config-service:v2 (canary 10%)

sophie: Canary applied. Monitoring effects on queue. Queue length dropping from 1200 -> 820. p95 latency improving slightly.

elsa-cs: Heads up — CS needs a short customer note for enterprise customers seeing degraded latency. ETA for update?

sophie: Tell them: partial degradation for large generations in eu-west1, best-effort reroute to us-central, no data loss, workaround: reduce max tokens or use embeddings for short tasks. I'll give an ETA after step 2.

raj: I'll handle step 2. Preparing routing change. Current routing state: 

```json
{"eu-west1": 0.85, "us-central": 0.10, "apac": 0.05}
```

raj: Will shift to `{"eu-west1": 0.4, "us-central": 0.55, "apac": 0.05}` over 2 minutes. Executing now.

deploy-bot: routing-service: weight update applied (eu-west1->0.4, us-central->0.55, apac->0.05)

sophie: After steering, observed: us-central absorbing traffic, but some requests still error with `variant_mismatch` on apac — we need to short-circuit rejects to try quantized variant.

maya: I can flip tolerant-variant-mode in router to auto-rewrite model ids for compatible variants. Risk: minor output quality variance. Recommend enabling for low-tier traffic only.

tom: Agreed. Enable for non-enterprise only. Command: 

```sh
curl -XPOST https://router.internal/tolerant-variant -d '{"enabled":true,"scope":"low_tier"}'
```

deploy-bot: tolerant-variant rollout started -> router:v1.3 (traffic-split: low_tier)

sophie: Now seeing apac rejects drop to near-zero. Queue down to ~210. p99 down to ~2.1s. Good progress.

infra-sre: Cloud ticket updated: GCP case 87654321 — asked for regional capacity; tentative ETA 28m for provisioning confirmations. Also requested quota increase for GPUs by +12.

elsa-cs: Drafting customer note for affected accounts. I'll include: scope, what we're doing, recommended mitigation, expected ETA. Need list of impacted enterprise accounts.

maya: I'll prepare impact list. Early look: ~14 enterprise orgs saw >5% error rate during peak; top 3 affected: Acme, NovaML, Finly.

raj: We're seeing some tail 429s from our own ingress because the global proxy started applying burst-throttles. I reduced proxy retry budget to avoid cascading overload.

sophie: Handing off to raj — I've stabilized the eu-west1 queue to <250 and throttles are in place. If anything spikes, escalate to infra-sre.

sophie: Handoff note -> next oncall: @raj. Key items: monitor queue, confirm quota bump, watch routing rollback if any model regressions reported by customers.

raj: Taking over. I'll watch dashboards for the next 2 hours.

elsa-cs: Draft for customers: 

"We experienced temporary capacity constraints in our eu-west1 inference pool resulting in increased latency and intermittent errors for some large-generation requests. We implemented traffic steering to alternate regions, temporary rate limits for low-tier plans, and tolerant-variant routing to reduce rejects. We expect full capacity restoration once additional GPUs are provisioned (~30-45m)."

elsa-cs: Can someone confirm the ETA to include? maya/infra-sre?

infra-sre: Provider ETA ~28-40m. I'll update if it changes.

tom: Creating incident record INC-2026-1843001. Owning team: Platform/Serving. Postmortem owners: maya + infra-sre. Severity: Sev-2 for hosted API (enterprise impact).

maya: Action items captured: 
- immediate: confirm quota bump, enable cross-zone provisioning, revert tolerant-variant after capacity restored.
- short: add pre-warming logic when queue > 500 to avoid hitting cloud capacity hard.
- long: improve routing compatibility matrix so fallback regions accept compatible variants automatically.

raj: Noting a couple follow-ups: traffic-steer runbook update (include tolerant-variant toggle), add per-region model inventory to router.

sophie: Adding one customer-facing note: advise reducing max_tokens for large gens to mitigate until quota is applied.

any-englead: Thanks team. Good mitigation and comms. Keep me posted if provider ETA slips >60m.

sophie: Closing thread for now — handing full monitoring to raj. Will reconvene for a postmortem after the incident. :thumbsup:

raj: Acknowledged. I'll update when GPUs come online or if queue rises >500 again.
